# Pianoers.com

> Independent reviews and guides for people learning piano: digital pianos and keyboards for beginners, online piano courses and apps, practice advice, piano care, and pianist biographies. Written by piano teachers Richard J. Abraham and Katarina. Some links on the site are affiliate links (Amazon and course providers); recommendations are not paid for.

Key pages:

- [Best beginner pianos and keyboards](https://pianoers.com/best-beginner-pianos/): the main buying guide, with a piano finder
- [Best digital pianos](https://pianoers.com/best-digital-piano/): digital pianos across budgets
- [Best online piano lessons](https://pianoers.com/best-piano-lessons-online/): online courses ranked
- [About Pianoers](https://pianoers.com/about/): who writes the site

## Learning piano

- [5 Best Piano Books for Adult Beginners (I've Tested Them All)](https://pianoers.com/best-piano-books-for-adult-beginners/): I tested every major piano method book.
- [5 Best Piano Methods To Learn Quickly](https://pianoers.com/5-best-piano-methods-to-learn-quickly/): Learn piano quickly!
- [How to learn piano by yourself: A Step-by-Step Guide](https://pianoers.com/teach-yourself-piano/): Teach yourself piano with a keyboard, one course, and 30 minutes a day.
- [Piano Basics: A Beginner's Guide to the Keyboard](https://pianoers.com/piano-basics-a-beginners-guide-to-the-keyboard/): Learn the piano keyboard in one sitting: 88 keys, where middle C is, what the black key groups mean, finger numbers 1-5, and how to set up C position.
- [Piano Practice: 4 Tips for Sessions That Work](https://pianoers.com/piano-practice-4-tips-to-successful-sessions/): How to practice piano so the time counts: one goal per session, a warm-up and cool-down split, chunked slow practice with a metronome ladder, and breaks.
- [Pianote Review 2026: The Honest Truth About Learning Piano With Video Lessons](https://pianoers.com/pianote-review/): Unbiased Pianote review 2026: real pricing, no real-time feedback, cluttered navigation, and mixed support.

## Piano care and maintenance

- [Are Piano Keys Still Made of Ivory?](https://pianoers.com/are-piano-keys-still-made-of-ivory/): No, piano keys are no longer made of ivory.
- [How The Piano Works: A Keypress Translated into Sound](https://pianoers.com/how-the-piano-works/): Discover exactly how a piano works, from keys and hammers to soundboard and strings.
- [How to Clean and Maintain Your Piano: A Concert Pianist's Guide to a Lifetime of Sound](https://pianoers.com/how-to-clean-and-maintain-your-piano/): Learn the essential steps to clean, protect, and prolong the life of your piano, from a professional concert pianist who treats her instrument like family.
- [How to Tune a Piano: A Simple Guide](https://pianoers.com/how-to-tune-a-piano-a-simple-guide/)
- [Piano Dehumidifier: Why Your Piano Needs One (And How to Choose the Right One)](https://pianoers.com/piano-dehumidifier-101-why-it-is-important/): Grand, upright, or digital piano, here’s everything you need to know about piano dehumidifiers: what they are, how to pick the right one, and how to use them without frying your in
- [Piano Humidifier: You Need To Keep Your Piano Hydrated](https://pianoers.com/piano-humidifier/): Protect your piano!
- [Piano Humidity and Temperature: The Ideal Range and How to Hold It](https://pianoers.com/climate-control-and-your-piano/): Keep a piano at 40 to 50% humidity and a steady 68 to 72°F.
- [Piano SOS: DIY Hacks for Keeping Your Instrument in Tune (Literally)](https://pianoers.com/piano-diy-repair-guide/): Is your piano sounding more like a clunker than a concert grand?
- [Piano Tuning: When and Why It's Needed](https://pianoers.com/piano-tuning-when-and-why-its-needed/): The secrets of piano tuning and why it's essential for optimal sound and longevity, explained by an accomplished concert pianist.
